book.t: In the Hebrew text chapter 4 is 3:19-24.

1:1.t: Malachi means "my messenger". He prophesied about 450-430 BC, in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah, when the returned exiles had grown careless in worship.

1:3.t: "Desert jackals": the KJV's "dragons of the wilderness".

1:11.t: "Will be great": the Hebrew has no verb and can be read "is great".

2:3.t: "Rebuke your descendants": the KJV's "corrupt your seed".

2:12.t: "Whoever he may be": the KJV's "the master and the scholar", a Hebrew idiom meaning "anyone at all".

2:15.t: "Has not the one God made you? You belong to Him in body and spirit": the KJV's "And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit." The Hebrew of this verse is very difficult.

2:16.t: "He hates divorce": the KJV's "he hateth putting away".

3:17.t: "My treasured possession": the KJV's "my jewels"; Hebrew segullah (Exodus 19:5).

4:6.t: "Total destruction": the KJV's "a curse"; Hebrew cherem, devotion to destruction.

1:2.t: "I have loved Jacob, but Esau I have hated": a Hebrew way of expressing choice. God chose Jacob's line for His covenant purposes, not Esau's. Paul quotes this in Romans 9:13.

2:7.t: "The messenger of the LORD of hosts" (Hebrew mal'akh): a priest's calling is to teach God's word faithfully.

3:1.t: "I will send My messenger, who will prepare the way before Me": Jesus identified this messenger as John the Baptist (Matthew 11:10). "The Lord you are seeking will come to His temple": the One who follows is the Lord Himself. Following this reading, His pronouns are capitalized in verses 1-3.

3:6.t: "I the LORD do not change": God's faithfulness, not Israel's, is why they still survive. Compare James 1:17.

3:10.t: "Test Me in this": the one place God invites His people to put Him to the test, by trusting Him with their giving.

4:2.t: "The Sun of righteousness will rise with healing in His wings": "wings" here are the rays of the rising sun. Charles Wesley's hymn "Hark! The Herald Angels Sing" applies this to Christ.

4:5.t: "I will send the prophet Elijah": the Old Testament closes with this promise. The angel Gabriel said John the Baptist would go "in the spirit and power of Elijah ... to turn the hearts of the parents to their children" (Luke 1:17), and Jesus confirmed it (Matthew 11:14, 17:10-13). After Malachi, God's prophetic voice was silent for about four hundred years until John appeared.
